subject: community-medicine
title: Medical entomology and insecticides: vectors, diseases and control

steps.tx: **Arthropods** transmit many human pathogens, so classifying them quickly matters. **Insects** have three pairs of legs and usually one or two pairs of wings. **Arachnids**, such as **hard ticks**, **soft ticks** and **trombiculid mites**, have four pairs of legs. **Crustaceans**, including the copepod **Cyclops**, carry five pairs. Recognising this **body plan** helps you identify a vector rapidly in an exam.
steps.say: Arthropods pass many infections to people, so sorting them quickly is useful. Insects possess three leg pairs and typically one or two wing pairs. Arachnids, including ticks and trombiculid mites, possess four leg pairs. Crustaceans such as Cyclops have five leg pairs. Remembering this body plan lets you place an unfamiliar vector into its class during an examination.

rows: Hard tick, soft tick, trombiculid mite

steps.tx: Vectors transmit infection in different ways. In **propagative** transmission the agent multiplies without changing form, as plague bacilli do in rat fleas. In **cyclopropagative** transmission the agent changes form and multiplies, as malaria does in mosquitoes. In **cyclodevelopmental** transmission the agent changes form only, as microfilariae do in mosquitoes. When the infection passes from an infected female to her offspring, this is **transovarian** transmission.

steps.tx: Louse-borne and flea-borne diseases are common exam topics. Lice transmit epidemic typhus, **relapsing fever** (epidemic) and trench fever, plus pediculosis. Rat fleas transmit plague and endemic (murine) typhus, caused by Rickettsia typhi. Soft ticks transmit endemic relapsing fever and Q fever. Hard ticks transmit tick typhus, Kyasanur forest disease and tick paralysis.

rows: Epidemic typhus, epidemic relapsing fever, trench fever

steps.tx: Larval control uses three approaches. Environmental control means intermittent irrigation and proper water management. Chemical control uses mineral oil, Paris green and synthetic larvicides. Biological control uses larvivorous fish such as **Gambusia** and Poecilia. Adult control uses residual spraying with DDT, BHC or malathion. Under the Indian toxicity labels, red means extremely toxic and green means slightly toxic.
